heading: Secrets
subtitle: Store passwords and keys on this device.

firstRun.title: Keep credentials out of your workflows
firstRun.body1: Secrets live in an encrypted vault on this Mac. A workflow step references a secret by name, and Mill fills in the value when the step runs.
firstRun.body2: Guardrails decide which steps may read each secret, and every read lands in the access history.

setup.heading: Store a password
setup.description: Keep passwords and keys in one encrypted vault on this device.

locked.heading: Vault is locked
locked.description: Unlock to view your saved passwords.
locked.keyMismatchHeading: This vault's key isn't on this device
locked.keyMismatchBody: The vault file was made with a key this device no longer has. Start a new vault to keep working; the old file stays beside it as a backup.
locked.restoreBackupCaption: Brings back the last backup's vault; it opens if its key is still on this device.

touchId.toggleCaption: Ask for Touch ID or your password before the vault opens in Mill.
touchId.unavailableCaption: Touch ID or a password isn't set up on this Mac.
touchId.requiredStatus: Touch ID or your password is required to unlock.

emptyDescription: Add a password to get started.

fields.title: Title
fields.sourceKeyCaption: Mill reads this key when something uses the secret, and never copies it here.

deleteConfirmBody: This permanently deletes "{{label}}". This cannot be undone.

accessHistory.heading: Access history
accessHistory.emptyDescription: Every time this vault is read, it shows up here.
accessHistory.readMcpServerSpawn: Read to start an MCP server
accessHistory.readConfigureToolsPreview: Read to list an MCP server's tools

reset.confirmBody: The current file is kept as a backup. Its entries can't be opened without the missing key.

sections.sourcesSubtitle: Read secrets from files and tools you already use.

noSourcesConfigured: Add a source under Sources first.

import.title: Import from an export
import.fileCaption: Export your passwords from the tool you use, then choose that file.
import.deleteCaption: The export holds every password in plain text.
